title: Reuse the GeoIMC middle-factor square root within inference
head: 1e0d50e49448c5496d50c2c8bf9cb3654d2a47d1
body:
### Description

GeoIMC computes the same middle-factor matrix square root twice in every inference call, once for row features and once for column features. This repeated decomposition dominates the measured small-query cases.

Compute it once and reuse it for both projections within that call. The scoring formula and transformations stay the same. Subsequent calls still recompute from the current weights, and the direct-embedding list path remains independent of the factor matrices.

Fixes #2468.

### Validation and performance

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43904653540) checks exact head `1e0d50e49448c5496d50c2c8bf9cb3654d2a47d1` with the documented Pymanopt revision:

- Python 3.10: NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1, Numba 0.57.1.
- Python 3.11: NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.13.1, Numba 0.61.2.
- Original GeoIMC tests: **12 passed**. Expanded equivalence suite: **26 passed** on both unchanged staging and the patch, without skips.
- Added checks cover float32/float64, filtered entity rows, all three score transformations, direct embeddings, unchanged input matrices and updated weights between calls.
- The complete inference benchmark uses five warmups and 31 alternating measurements with one BLAS thread. Every paired output is bitwise identical within its environment, and square-root calls decrease from two to one.

Python 3.11 runner results for fixed synthetic feature matrices:

| Scenario | Rank | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 943 users × 1,682 items, 128 features | 8 | 2.697 ms | 2.572 ms | 1.05× |
| 1 user × 256 items, 128 features | 32 | 0.686 ms | 0.388 ms | 1.77× |
| 1 user × 256 items, 256 features | 128 | 14.220 ms | 7.366 ms | 1.93× |

The other dependency environment gives 1.04×, 1.77× and 1.91× for the same shapes. These measurements are fixture-specific: large low-rank batches spend most of their time outside the square-root decomposition.

Black and `git diff --check` pass. Benchmark code, all individual timing samples, dependency versions and test logs are included in the validation branch and run artifacts.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads and 69 pre-existing fork branches, including nine reachable GeoIMC prediction source versions from 48 commits and their former paths. All factor-based variants compute the square root separately for both projections; the earlier fork top-k changes are unrelated.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Equivalence cases registered in the experimental CPU test group.
- [x] Code comment describes the shared factor within an inference call.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.
